items.title: The standard product torus as a compact Lie group
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. For $r\geq0$, let
$T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ with the quotient topology and coordinatewise
addition. On each circle factor, for every open interval $I\subset\mathbb R$
of length less than $1$, use the chart
$q(I)\to I$ given by the unique lift through the quotient map
$q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$; give $T$ the product smooth structure.
Write $\mathfrak t=T_0T$. For $1\leq i\leq r$, let $e_i$ be the tangent vector
at $0$ to the one-parameter subgroup
$s\mapsto(0,\ldots,[s],\ldots,0)$ in the $i$th coordinate. These vectors form
the period-one basis of $\mathfrak t$, and $e_i^*$ denotes its dual basis.
The standard Lie exponential is normalized by
$\exp_T(s e_i)=(0,\ldots,[s],\ldots,0)$ for every $s\in\mathbb R$.
For $r=0$, use the one-point group and the empty basis. This convention makes
$T$ a compact connected abelian Lie group, hence a torus in the sense of the
standard compact-Lie-group definition; its identity inclusion is a cofibration,
so this based group is well-pointed.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: Chapter 0, “Cell Complexes” and “Operations on Spaces,” printed pp. 5–8: the circle cell structure, product cells, and the product topology for finite cell complexes.

items.title: Real cohomology of the chosen torus classifying space
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $r\geq0$, let
$T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$, and fix its displayed product decomposition. For
each factor use the standard quotient Lie-group smooth structure and
period-one tangent basis. Identify $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ with the
multiplicative unit circle by $\epsilon([t])=e^{2\pi i t}$ and transfer its
right action to Milnor's countable-join model $E_{S^1}$; put
$ET=(E_{S^1})^r$ with the coordinatewise right $T$-action and set $BT=ET/T$.
Let $e_i\in\mathfrak t$ be the period-one tangent vector in the $i$th circle
factor and $e_i^*$ its dual. Let $u=e(\gamma_{\mathbb R})$ be the integral
degree-two generator of $H^*(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty};\mathbb Z)$ defined by the
complex orientation of the real rank-two bundle underlying the tautological
complex line, and let $u_{\mathbb R}$ be its image under change of coefficients
$\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R$. Under the product quotient identification
$BT\cong(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r$, write $u_i$ for the pullback of
$u_{\mathbb R}$ from the $i$th factor. Then
$$H^*(BT;\mathbb R)\cong\mathbb R[u_1,\ldots,u_r],\qquad |u_i|=2,$$
and the chosen identification $e_i^*\mapsto u_i$ is a graded-algebra
isomorphism from $\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}(\mathfrak t^*)$, with its
linear generators assigned degree two. For $r=0$, both rings are $\mathbb R$.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: §3.2, Theorem 3.19, printed pp. 221–222: the integral cohomology rings of finite and infinite complex projective space.

items.title: Borel and Cartan equivariant cohomology for a compact torus
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ be a compact torus with its standard product Lie-group smooth structure and period-one basis, and let $M$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, not assumed compact, with a smooth left action $a:T\times M\to M$. Work over $\mathbb R$ and use the chosen product Milnor model $ET=(E_{S^1})^r$ and $BT=ET/T$ from the preceding coefficient lemma. Give $ET\times M$ the right diagonal action $(e,p)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,t^{-1}\cdot p)$ and define
$$ET\times_T M:=(ET\times M)/T.$$
The **Borel equivariant cohomology** is the graded ring
$$H_T^*(M;\mathbb R):=H_{\mathrm{sing}}^*(ET\times_T M;\mathbb R).$$
For $M=\{\ast\}$ this gives $H_T^*(\ast;\mathbb R)=H^*(BT;\mathbb R)$; the selected degree-two normalization in $\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}(\mathfrak t^*)$ is the isomorphism established in the preceding coefficient lemma.

The quotient map $q:ET\times M\to ET\times_T M$ and projection
$\pi([e,p])=[e]$ give the associated-space square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}ET\times M&\xrightarrow{q}&ET\times_T M\\\downarrow\operatorname{pr}_1&&\downarrow\pi\\ET&\xrightarrow{q_T}&BT\end{array}$$
Its TikZ source is
```latex
\begin{tikzcd}
ET\times M \arrow[r,"q"] \arrow[d,"\operatorname{pr}_1"'] & ET\times_T M \arrow[d,"\pi"]\\
ET \arrow[r,"q_T"'] & BT
\end{tikzcd}
```
where $q_T:ET\to BT$ is the orbit quotient. The projection $\pi$ is
well-defined because $[e\cdot t]=[e]$ for every $t\in T$. The square
commutes because both composites send $(e,p)$ to $[e]$.

Let $\mathfrak t=T_eT$, with basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ and dual basis $u_1,\ldots,u_r$. Regard $\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}(\mathfrak t^*)$ as a polynomial algebra by assigning each linear generator degree two. Use the trivial $T$-action on this polynomial factor, and the induced left action $t\cdot\alpha=(a_{t^{-1}})^*\alpha$ on forms. It is a left action because pullback reverses composition: $a_{t^{-1}}^*a_{s^{-1}}^*=(a_{s^{-1}}\circ a_{t^{-1}})^*=a_{(ts)^{-1}}^*$. The **Cartan complex** is the graded-commutative algebra
$$C_T(M):=\bigl(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}(\mathfrak t^*)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\Omega^*(M)\bigr)^T,$$
with multiplication $(P\otimes\alpha)(Q\otimes\beta)=PQ\otimes(\alpha\wedge\beta)$, where $\wedge$ is the differential-form wedge product and all tensor products are algebraic. The superscript denotes the fixed subspace for the diagonal action, and a polynomial of degree $j$ tensored with a $k$-form has total degree $2j+k$. For $\xi\in\mathfrak t$, use the library fundamental vector field
$$X_\xi(p)=\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}\exp_T(-s\xi)\cdot p.$$
On polynomial-valued forms define the degree-one Cartan operator
$$d_T(P\otimes\alpha)=P\otimes d\alpha-\sum_{i=1}^r(u_iP)\otimes\iota_{X_{e_i}}\alpha,$$
extended linearly. The tensor $\sum_i u_i\otimes X_{e_i}$ is basis-independent. The **Cartan equivariant cohomology** in this item means $H^*(C_T(M),d_T)$; the proof below establishes $d_T^2=0$ on $C_T(M)$.

This definition does not assert a general isomorphism between the Borel and Cartan cohomology rings. It defines neither equivariant Chow groups nor equivariant quotient-stack Borel–Moore homology, and no rational-coefficient comparison is being used in the real Cartan complex.

title: Borel and Cartan Equivariant Cohomology — Examples

items.title: The Borel and Cartan cohomology of a point
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement: Assume AC and let $T=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ act trivially on the one-point smooth manifold $\{\ast\}$. Use the period-one tangent generator and its selected degree-two polynomial generator $u$. In the chosen Borel model, $H_T^*(\{\ast\};\mathbb R)\cong\mathbb R[u]$, with $|u|=2$. The Cartan complex is $\mathbb R[u]$ with zero differential, so its cohomology is also $\mathbb R[u]$ under the selected coefficient normalization.

references.title: Jonas Menzi and Finn Michler, A Brief Introduction to Equivariant Cohomology
references.locator: Example 2.4 (Borel model) and Example 2.22 (Cartan model), PDF pp. 3 and 7.

items.title: The free translation action of the circle on itself
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $T=M=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$, with $T$ acting on $M$ by left translation $t\cdot[x]=[t+x]$. Use the period-one tangent generator $e$, so the library convention gives $X_e=-\partial_x$, and let $\eta$ be the global one-form on $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ descended from $-dx$ on $\mathbb R$. In the chosen Borel model the map $[v,x]\mapsto v\cdot x$ identifies $ET\times_TT$ with $ET$, hence $H_T^0(T;\mathbb R)=\mathbb R$ and $H_T^k(T;\mathbb R)=0$ for $k>0$. The invariant Cartan complex is $\mathbb R[u]\oplus\mathbb R[u]\eta$, with $|u|=2$, $|\eta|=1$, $d_TP(u)=0$, and $d_T(P(u)\eta)=-uP(u)$. Its cohomology is $\mathbb R$ in degree zero and zero in positive degrees, agreeing with the Borel calculation for this action.
